svg.title: A picnic that works for everyone

text.tspan: People share food during an outing.
A picnic that works for everyone
A picnic is more fun when friends plan ahead and help each other. Our picnic near the lake on
First, a clear plan helps us prepare. We are going to meet at ten. I am going to bring
sandwiches, Lina can bring fruit, and Omar can bring water. Everyone knows what to do.
Second, helping each other makes the work easier. Omar has a heavy bag, so we take turns
carrying it. After lunch, we all help to clean up.
Planning and helping make our picnic a good day for everyone. We enjoy our food and our
time together. Next time, we want to work together again.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Ask a friend to help you share a meal. Explain two things you can do together. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two
developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: say what you want to do; explain the first step; explain a
different second step; say why the two steps help.)
